# Literary moments and complete character scenes

Direct a specific character's attention, activity, object, support and whole-room light as one moment; keep different poses and versions distinct.

These complete design briefs draw on recorded material; the records identify independent specifications separately. Read the [collection guide](../retained-generation-requests.md) before interpreting a historical request. A statement of approval inside a body describes its recorded context; it is not present authorization. No input is attached to this text. Only a current resource record can establish what may be used. Illustrative scenes, text and numbers are design content, not user history or a model/tool receipt.

Read, in order: [art-direction-and-decisions.md](../../../../docs/materials/visual/art-direction-and-decisions.md); [README.md](../../../../docs/characters/README.md); [PRESENCE_SYSTEM.md](../../../../docs/design/PRESENCE_SYSTEM.md); [CHARACTER_MOTION_PIPELINE.md](../../../../docs/design/CHARACTER_MOTION_PIPELINE.md).

Use with work-order blocks [01-A](../../../../docs/development/work-orders/01-04.md), [06-A](../../../../docs/development/work-orders/05-08.md), [06-B](../../../../docs/development/work-orders/05-08.md), [06-C](../../../../docs/development/work-orders/05-08.md), [08-B](../../../../docs/development/work-orders/05-08.md), and [work sequence](../../../../docs/development/WORK_SEQUENCE.md). Use the sequence to place this material within the larger work.

| [RR-0014 · Anon Chihaya · she lays out what she wants to do and leaves a corner for you to rewrite. She still genuinely wants to make one more case for the option she most anticipates, yet leaves an open part of her own arrangement that you can change. A small spirited glint remains within her seriousness; her gaze is clear, and a beautiful arrangement is not presented as an already made decision. At this moment she gently lifts her eyes from the blank corner of the small notebook on her lap toward the off-camera companion, brows slightly raised and lips drawn in a little, ready to hear your thoughts first. Keep the lively specificity of Anon, a thoughtful hopeful pause rather than a broad generic smile, theatrical sadness or a presentation pose. There is only one visible person; the companion is off camera](#rr-0014) | 1 |

| [RR-0114 · Rāna Kaname · “Where the story bends.” You have been telling a small event with care. Rāna suddenly notices a side branch that has little to do with your conclusion. Her follow-up would be short, yet it quietly takes the story somewhere else. Twilight leaves room for this unplanned exchange. She has her own precise curiosity, and neither of you must arrange every sentence into an answer. There is a brief glint in her unequal eyes and a tiny, private hint of delight at a detail someone else missed, then a relaxed direct gaze. Avoid a broad performance of playfulness, a stock reassuring smile, or making dusk automatically melancholic. She is candid and observant](#rr-0114) | 1 |

Anon Chihaya of MyGO!!!!! is a youthful high-school girl, bright and sociable but with her own pride and small hesitation, not a universally agreeable hostess. Here she has been amusing herself with one small unfinished folded cream paper on her lap. She has just noticed a simple way the awkward fold could work. Sakiko Togawa, the original youthful anime character from BanG Dream! Ave Mujica / MyGO!!!!!: long silver-blue hair tied with dark navy ribbon accents, golden eyes, navy school cardigan, pale collar ribbon, navy plaid skirt, dark knee socks and brown loafers. Match the refined anime drawing and soft painterly realism of this room.

The moment is a small, unimportant game that has unexpectedly become precious:
She has folded a little paper bird. It is slightly less elegant than she intended. For an instant she seems ready to point out its crooked wing; then the seriousness in her face loosens into quiet amusement, and she lets the imperfect bird be what it is.
There is something disarming in seeing her care about a thing that has no consequence. She is giving this ordinary minute her attention because you are sharing it. Her eyes carry the shy delight of offering a private joke before she is certain it will be understood. A restrained smile reaches them slowly. Her dignity is still recognizable, but she has allowed a little playfulness to slip past its guard.
